mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen each of the last three weeks (-46.0 to -40.6). This momentum reflects gradual re-engagement with shopping and dining as workplace mobility stabilizes, and the trend is expected to continue upward over the next four weeks absent a shock.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose from -46.0 to -40.6 over the last three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to average higher over the next 28 days than the last 28 days despite the prior three-week rising streak.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility dropped sharply from 49.0 to 27.3 in the most recent week, likely reflecting cooling weather or reduced outdoor appeal. This displaced outdoor recreation substitutes toward indoor retail and recreation venues, pushing RETAIL_REC upward over the following week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 15 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS dropped from 49.0 to 27.3 in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week following a PARKS drop exceeding 15 points, or PARKS rebounds instead of staying low.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT have both remained nearly flat for four weeks (around -46 and -54 respectively). Their joint stability indicates a settled commuting baseline that sustains steady weekday retail footfall, keeping RETAIL_REC on its gradual upward path over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both remain within ±2 points of current levels for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES held near -46 and TRANSIT near -54 across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines over the next 28 days even though WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both stayed within the stated stability band.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL mobility rises sharply while WORKPLACES simultaneously falls, this joint shift signals renewed government restrictions or public caution driving people back indoors, which would reverse the recent RETAIL_REC uptrend into decline over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises more than 3 points while WORKPLACES falls more than 5 points within one week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL and WORKPLACES have been stable but could shift with new restrictions
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise over the next 28 days even after RESIDENTIAL and WORKPLACES jointly cross the stated thresholds.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has drifted slightly more negative (-19.1 to -20.4), consistent with the tail-off of pandemic-driven stockpiling behavior. As essential-goods trips normalize downward, discretionary spending capacity shifts toward retail and recreation, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM declined from -19.1 to -20.4 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days despite GROCERY_PHARM continuing its gradual decline.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT has remained persistently depressed near -54, indicating sustained avoidance of public transport. If TRANSIT falls further below -55, this signals renewed commuter caution that caps footfall to retail districts reliant on transit access, slowing or reversing RETAIL_REC growth.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -55 points for at least one week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT has hovered between -53.3 and -55.6 over the last four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC still rises over the next 14 days even after TRANSIT drops below -55 points.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous drop in PARKS alongside flat RESIDENTIAL mobility suggests people are redirecting outdoor leisure time into indoor retail and recreation activity rather than staying home, producing a short-term boost in RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 10 points while RESIDENTIAL stays within ±1 point
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell 21.7 points week-on-week while RESIDENTIAL stayed near 13
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC shows no increase in the week following a PARKS drop with stable RESIDENTIAL, or RESIDENTIAL also rises materially.

mechanism_narrative: In a continued reopening regime, further easing of workplace restrictions would be reflected in a sustained rise in WORKPLACES mobility, which in turn drives higher RETAIL_REC over the subsequent four weeks via restored commuter-linked shopping trips.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises more than 5 points over two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES has been flat near -46 for four weeks, leaving room for policy-driven recovery
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 28 days even after WORKPLACES increases by more than 5 points over two weeks.
